content.thinking:
I'm thinking through realistic proportions for the red panda relative to a mossy boulder, and imagining the pose: the panda balanced on top with four legs, tail curved for balance, giving it a natural, dynamic stance.

For the Genshin-style treatment I'll add cel shading and gold filigree accents, leaning into a Dendro theme—glowing green-yellow particles, small flowers and gold/teal runes carved into the stone, plus a small golden pendant on a red ribbon collar with tassels for the panda. I'm settling on proportions too: head-body around 0.55m, tail 0.45m, shoulder height roughly 0.28m, with moderate chibi-style scaling for the head and eyes.

Now I'm working out the overall composition size and coordinates—stone roughly 0.75m long and 0.3m tall, panda adding another 0.3m so the whole piece sits around 0.65-0.8m total with the tail raised. I'm placing the panda facing forward along z, centered over the stone, and thinking through building the stone as a faceted low-poly form from overlapping scaled icospheres to get a mottled, irregular rock look.

I'm figuring out the stone's shape as a flattened, dome-topped boulder using a scaled sphere, then calculating the exact surface heights where the panda's feet will land so they rest naturally on the curved top.

For better realism I'm switching to an icosahedron geometry with deterministic noise-based vertex displacement to give the stone a rougher, more natural look, while making sure the displacement stays consistent across shared vertices. I also need to add smaller moss-covered stones around the base and ensure the whole formation sits flush with the floor at y=0.

Working through the boulder shape, I realize a simple sphere scale would sink below the floor, so instead I'm building a dome-like profile using a lathe geometry with a bulging base that tapers upward, giving it a believable boulder silhouette. Since lathe geometry alone would look too regular, I'm planning a custom buffered geometry built from latitude rings where each vertex radius gets perturbed by a seeded noise function for organic irregularity.

Now I'm shifting to the panda's anatomy — sketching out the spine chain positions starting at the hips, figuring out leg length for a stout red panda stance (~0.14m from belly to ground), and estimating body radius (~0.09m) to account for a thick fluffy build, so I can place the spine height correctly relative to the stone's surface.

I'm also thinking through overall proportions: giving the head a slight enlargement (~1.2x real scale) for a chibi-ish look, keeping the body around 0.5m long, and posing the panda in a slight crouch with front legs spread for balance and the tail curled up in an S shape. Starting the skeleton with the hips as root near [0, 0.45, -0.17] and beginning the spine chain from there.

Building the spine and neck chain next...

Simplifying to a single neck span with a head joint parented to it, then adding a jaw joint as a child of the head. For the head shape itself, I'm thinking wide with white fluffy cheek tufts to match the Genshin red panda look.

For facial details, I'm planning a white muzzle with a small black nose, big rounded triangular ears with white inner fur, dark tear-mark stripes from eyes to mouth, white eyebrow spots, and a rusty orange forehead. For the eyes I want big anime-style decal eyes rather than small realistic red panda eyes, leaning toward an amber-gold iris color with a subtle blush overlay to keep the cute Genshin aesthetic.

Now I'm working out the head geometry — placing the skull as a scaled sphere attached near the head joint, wider than tall to capture the round red panda face shape, with the face oriented forward. I'm adding a smaller white snout sphere for the muzzle, a tiny dark nose at the tip, and a separate lower jaw piece so the mouth reads as closed.

For the fur details, I'm adding small pointed cones along the cheeks for the characteristic spiky tufts, plus a forehead tuft. The ears I'm considering as flattened, tilted spheres or extruded rounded triangles with a darker outer surface and lighter inner fur patch, angled outward to read as alert and expressive.

Working out the ear orientation vectors so the normal faces forward while tilting outward slightly, like real cupped red panda ears, adjusting the axis components to get that forward-outward lean on both sides.

Now I'm thinking through the inner-ear white patch placement and how to detect which face is front based on the thickness vector dot product. For body colors, I'm mapping the Genshin-style palette: a brighter orange back, dark-brown belly and legs, and cream face markings, with cel-shaded tones layered on top.

For the body shading, I'm applying a zigzag fur-edge transition between the orange back and dark belly tones with cel-shading thresholds based on normal direction against the key light. Then I'm laying out the body shape as a loft along the spine with stations defining width and height at each point—larger at the haunches, tapering toward the chest—skinned to the spine chain and hips.

Now I'm working through the skeleton structure: defining a root hip joint, then a spine chain running from hips through mid-body to chest, with a separate tail chain branching back from the hips, and sweeping the body mesh along a catmull path through these points.

For legs, I'm sketching out the shoulder placement and planning inverse-kinematics limbs so the forepaws can reach a balance pose with elbows bent and paws angled slightly outward toward the floor.

I'm planning to tag the paw tip joint with a leg role, then sprout toes as separate digit joints rather than non-joint parts, giving each paw three toe joints spread out in the rest pose.

Scaling this up, I'll settle on four visible digit joints per paw, parented to the paw tip, each with a small capsule sweep for the toe shape — totaling sixteen digit joints across all legs, plus small claw spikes at the tips.

For leg skinning I'm tapering the tube radius down the limb chain, thicker at the shoulder and narrowing toward the wrist before widening slightly at the paw, with darker fur stockings and cel-shading overlaid. For the hind legs I'm positioning the hip joint and working through a multi-segment limb (thigh, knee, hock, sole) to get the plantigrade stance right, considering whether to use a simpler two-segment chain plus a forward sole piece instead of four full segments.

Checking the reach: hip at height 0.40 drops to foot height around 0.30, a vertical difference of 0.10, while the foot itself spans about 0.08 horizontally from heel to toe. I'm verifying that the combined thigh and shin lengths of 0.16 can actually span the distance from hip to heel given these offsets.

This gives a slightly crouched stance with a knee that protrudes forward, which looks fine. Now I need to figure out stone contact — I should determine the floor height from the stone's surface geometry, but there's a rigging problem: the stone is static while the panda has a skeleton, and a rig can only have one root joint. I'm considering making a separate root joint like "base" positioned at the origin, with "hips" as its child, so the stone and panda can coexist under one hierarchy.

Following the typical convention where hips are the first spine joint under a root, I'll name the root joint "root" and keep hips as its child. For the tail, I'm designing a bushy ringed red panda tail about 0.45-0.5 long, arched upward in an S-curve behind the body for balance, with varying radius (thicker at base, tapering to a point) and alternating orange/rust ring stripes painted along its length using a banding function based on position along the tail, ending in a cream tip.

I'm refining the ring bands with zigzag edges between colors for a fur-like texture, considering adding small fluff spikes or a tuft at the tail tip, and layering in dendro-themed glow accents -- floating leaf-shaped particles and a carved glowing sigil ring on the stone. For accessories, I'm planning a crimson ribbon collar with a gold bell and tassels, plus gold filigree details to tie into the Genshin aesthetic.

Now I'm adding a gold tail-ring with a teal gem and a gold ear stud with a tassel, then designing a decal-based gold-teal rune pattern on the stone's front face with glowing emissive sections. I'm also planning moss clusters, grass tufts, tiny ferns, flowers, and small toadstool mushrooms scattered across the stone's top and sides for texture and color variety.

For the stone's base coloring, I'm using a grey-lilac Genshin-style palette with a warmer lighter top and violet shadows, then building a paint function that blends moss and stone using noise-driven zigzag edges along one axis so the transition looks organic rather than sharp, wrapping it all in cel shading for the toon look.

I'm adding crack details using cell-based distance differences to create darker thin lines across the stone surface, then adjusting the panda's pose to feel more "balancing" by widening the stance and raising the tail, with paws positioned near the edges of a smaller stone base to sell the precarious footing.

Working out dome geometry for the stone, computing surface heights at the paw positions, and realizing a plain ellipsoid feels too smooth -- switching to a superellipsoid-style profile to give the boulder a squarer, more natural rock shape.

I'll space rings using sine spacing to cluster more near the edge, then add noise-based radial and height perturbation for a faceted boulder look, settling on 7 rings with 14 segments.

For the moss, I'm adding flattened sphere lumps along the top rim plus hanging card tufts, grass blade cards, and small fern leaves, and I'm now thinking about whether to give the panda fur similar spiky card tufts along its cheeks and flanks.

Now I'm turning to the eyes, placing an anime-style eye decal on the skull sphere using surface mapping, sizing each eye to roughly 0.045 by 0.058 relative to a 0.16-wide head and positioning them at a slight azimuth and elevation offset to match the red panda's dark iris coloring.

I'm layering in the facial markings next: dark eye rims, cream eyebrow spots as tiny spheres, and the characteristic tear-line stripes running from the inner eye down the muzzle, computing these by defining coordinates relative to the head center so I can paint region-based masks for the red panda's cream muzzle and cheek markings.

I'm also considering the rusty band across the forehead down toward the nose bridge, plus the white muzzle with black nose, dark tear marks, and white eyebrow patches that define the red panda's facial markings.

Now I'm working out the geometric conditions for the rust-colored stripe between the eyes and the slanted tear marks running from under the eyes toward the mouth corners, using distance-based checks on the coordinates.

I still need the head's absolute position in model space to anchor these details properly. Given how dense this region is, I'll write a first draft and plan to check it against a preview before refining the color palette further.

Defining more cel colors...

For the collar, I'm thinking of sweeping a red scarf ribbon around the neck joint geometry, checking if the neck itself is built as a sweep I can loop around.

I need to make sure the loop cuts cleanly where the neck bone starts inside the chest, since that joint may be capped and the smallest surrounding loop should trace only the neck tube's own surface rather than the chest body.

Setting up imports and starting the code...

Still shaping boulder geometry...

Building vertex and triangle indices for the ring geometry...

For the quad strip between inner ring A and outer ring B, I'm checking winding by plugging in screen coordinates for a sample angle to confirm the triangle order (A_i, B_i, B_{i+1}) gives the correct upward-facing normal.

I'm planning the boulder cluster: a main stone with two smaller stones offset behind-left and front-right, plus scattered pebbles, all sharing the same stone/moss material. I'm keeping vertex jitter radial and subtle so the top stays flat enough for paw placement, and setting up a surface query to cast rays for positioning feet on the rock.

Now I'm mapping the skeleton: a root joint with a spine-role hips joint, then a neck chain leading to the head, jaw, and hinge-role ear joints, plus a tail chain. I'm weighing whether to add thin whisker sweeps for detail but considering skipping them due to tessellation issues at that thinness.

For the head geometry, I'm planning the skull, a cream-painted muzzle sphere with a small dark glossy nose, and a jaw sphere with a thin ink sweep marking the mouth line and philtrum.

I'm also adding cheek tufts as cone spikes on both sides, using consistent cel-paint colors for the fur, plus ears built with extrusion and an inner paint detail, including a small gold earring torus on the left ear.

Then I move to the eyes, eyebrow spots, white brow tufts, a small rust forehead tuft, and whiskers, skipping teeth for now. For the body, I'm thinking through a teal cord scarf with gold bell and tassels to contrast against the orange fur, and shaping the hind haunch with a scaled sphere for the hip.

For legs I'm using the darker plum-brown tone with a boundary line where haunch meets shoulder, plus small capsule toes with cream claws on the paws. For the tail I'm alternating rust and darker red rings with a dark brown tip, considering a gold band near the base.

Thinking more Genshin-themed, I'm adding a small gold filigree ring accessory around the tail with a tiny gem, plus a scattering of glowing green-yellow leaf-shaped dendro particles floating in a spiral near the tail and shoulders to evoke that elemental glow motif.

I'll also sketch in extra details: a glowing gem pendant, faint glowing runes etched onto the stone base, and tiny mushrooms with teal glowing caps sprouting from it for extra flavor, along with a circular ornate rune design—gold ring outline with swirling teal dendro leaves and small diamond accents—to decorate the stone surface.

I'm placing this rune decal on the stone's front-facing side, letting it glow with its own golden color so the engraved lines appear lit from within, Genshin-style. I'm also considering adding a shimenawa-like gold rope wrapped around the boulder as an offering marker.

Working out rope twist spiral math...

Now I'm planning the shide paper streamers hanging from the rope — zigzag white paper with fold lines, sized appropriately, placed at several points along the front, plus gold cord and red tassel decorations. I'm starting to build the shide SVG with a zigzag polygon shape and light gray fold lines.

Still writing SVGs... I'm sketching the remaining texture assets: a mossy grass tuft with lighter blade tips, the rune decal, a grey fur tuft, and a small daisy-like flower with white petals and yellow center to scatter on moss or stand upright on stems.

For mushrooms, I'm planning a simple lathe-based cap and stem with a spotted cel pattern, placing two or three near the stone base, plus scattering small pebbles for extra detail. I'm also starting to write a helper function for the panda's paw toes.

Writing joint positions...

Hind foot sweeps roughly 0.08-0.09 long with shortened last segment and a few toe capsules past the tip. I'm tallying up the full joint count across spine, ears, tail, legs and toes to roughly 55, and noting I'll need the stone's top position computed before finalizing body placement.

Working out the Y0 reference from a raycast against the stone's surface, then deriving shoulder, belly, and paw positions relative to that height so the body sits naturally low with proper clearance above the ground.

Checking the shoulder-to-paw distance against limb segment lengths to confirm the arm is reachable with a backward elbow bend, then considering splaying the front paws wider since the geometry feels too tight.

Checking heel and toe placements against hip, the distances stay under the leg length bound so the bend works geometrically. I'm reconsidering whether the leg clearance should be 0.21 or 0.17, settling on 0.155 for body height given the red panda's short stubby legs.

Now I'm laying out the spine path from rump through hips, mid, chest, to neckbase, with a slight arch, and deciding how to chain the spine joints — treating hips as the root-adjacent spine joint and building spine1/spine2/chest tip from there, parented appropriately under the root.

Next I'm defining the neck chain parented to chest, running from chest to a head-base point, with the head joint tilted slightly and positioned so its center and snout tip sit forward along the local z-axis. Then I'm setting up the body sweep along a catmull path through rump, hips, mid, chest, and neckbase with varying cross-section radii (rump smallest, hips and mid wider), letting the neck tube overlap slightly with both body and head.

I'm deciding the body path should terminate at the chest tip, with a separate neck tube extension so joint ownership along the spine chain stays clean -- chest owns anything past spine2. For coloring, I'm applying a cel-shaded fur edge paint (rust over deep tones) with a normal-based threshold controlling where the fur "teeth" pattern appears.

Now I'm tuning that same fur-edge logic across body regions: lowering the level threshold slightly so belly and legs read as dark while sides keep the rust tone, then setting haunches/shoulders with a steeper split so outer surfaces stay rust and inner surfaces go dark. For the legs, I'm switching to a position-based fur paint so the upper leg gets a rust zigzag while the lower leg stays solid dark.

I'm also considering a whimsical touch — a tiny glowing leaf sprout on the panda's head between the ears, like a dendro accent — plus working out the tail's curved path coordinates relative to the hips so it arcs upward and forward naturally.

Writing tail radius and joint data...

Now I'm thinking about adding a gold ring band around the tail at a point along its curve, keeping it simple without tassels or gems, and scattering tinted fur tuft cards on the flanks and hind cheeks for extra texture.

For the fur cards, I'm planning around 40 on the body colored by the coat paint and 40 on the tail colored by the ring paint sampled at each card's root, so the tail rings continue naturally through the fur. The cards are cheap to render and will shade using the hit normal for realistic lighting.

Skipping the chest ruff since red pandas lack a bib, but adding a bell at the collar for a nice detail. For ambient glow, I'm scattering about 9 dendro leaves with varied tilt and spin near the tail using a seeded random generator, plus roughly 14 tiny glowing firefly spheres in a yellow-green tone merged into a single part, and adding flattened moss lumps using low-poly spheres for stone surface detail.

I need to scatter about 26 moss lumps on the stone surface, but I have to filter them out near where the panda's paws land so they don't sink into the moss -- filtering by distance from the paw target points. After that I'm scattering around 60 grass cards onto upward-facing stone surfaces.

I'm also adding grass cards sized small with slight lean and crossed geometry, avoiding the paws, plus a few flower cards near the rim and mushroom sticks scattered around. For the hanging moss fringe along the sides, I'm picking hits where the surface normal faces more sideways and placing drooping frame cards with a simple lobed strand shape to suggest hanging vines.

For the stone surface itself, I'm defining a paint function that uses cell noise to create cracks and a secondary noise layer to blend between two stone tones, then layering moss coverage on top based on normal direction and noise so it concentrates more on upward-facing surfaces, with a threshold determining where stone gives way to moss coloring. I'm weighing whether the cell-noise cost per texel is acceptable at the texture resolution I'm baking to.

I'm making the moss two-toned by mixing light and dark moss colors via noise for variation near edges, then wrapping it all in a lighting function that darkens shaded areas using the surface normal relative to the light direction.

Now I'm working out the gem pendant: a glowing teal octahedron paired with a small gold bell shape (a tiny sphere with a thin dark slit torus), and I need to figure out where to anchor it on the collar geometry -- picking the front-lower point of the neck loop by offsetting from its center using the ring's radius.

I'm realizing the collar placement conflicts with the head, since the skull extends back far enough to overlap the collar at that neck position, so I'm reconsidering hanging the pendant lower on the chest instead, using a chest-front point on the body's sweep surface rather than the neck ring.

Deciding to simplify by using a thick circular cord cross-section instead of fighting with frame orientation for the scarf.

For the eyes, I want that big shiny anime look fitting a Genshin-style red panda character, so I'm sizing them fairly large relative to the head width and positioning them symmetrically on the face.

Now I'm working out the head's absolute coordinates, placing the head base and skull center with a slight forward offset, and defining the skull as a low-poly sphere with smooth shading for the toon-style cel look.

I'm checking texel density for the baked cel shading texture to ensure enough resolution for sharp paint boundaries at roughly 2mm per texel, and sketching where the cream-colored patches land on the skull's front and cheeks.

For the face paint function, I'm defining a normalized local coordinate around the head center and setting up the rust-colored cap region using a zigzag boundary line, with cream covering the rest of the face except for dark tear marks, while the back of the head gets a different base color.

Still refining facial markings...

I'll skip the painted eyebrow spots since the anime eye already has its own brow, keeping just the tear mark. For the muzzle, I'm positioning a cream-colored sphere forward of the skull center with its own scale so it protrudes correctly, then placing a small ellipsoid nose just above it, checking that the muzzle front and nose positions line up properly in z and y.

For the mouth, I'm sketching a lower jaw sphere positioned and scaled to sit under the muzzle, then trying to work out the philtrum and mouth-fork line as a polyline along the muzzle surface, but I'm having trouble pinning exact coordinates by eye and deciding to just approximate and verify visually in preview rather than compute exact surface points.

Instead I'll draw the mouth as two thin curved ink sweeps from the base of the philtrum outward to the sides, using a catmull curve with small radius tubes, and drape them onto the muzzle/jaw surface so they sit correctly at the seam where the two parts meet.

For cheek tufts, I'm placing three stacked spikes per side near the cheek, varying their base offsets, lengths, and tilt directions to give a layered fluffy look. Now for the ears, I'm shaping them as large triangular red panda ears with rounded tips, positioned at the upper sides of the skull and tilted slightly forward.

Next I'm adding thin tapered whisker spikes near the muzzle in a cream color, keeping the mesh simple since detail isn't critical there. I'm skipping an inner mouth or tongue, and setting up decal weighting so eye parts bind correctly to the head bone. Finally I'm considering a small charming touch -- a tuft of rust-colored spikes on the forehead plus a tiny glowing leaf sprout between the ears with a swept stem.

Need to avoid `any` and ReturnType typing issues, so I'll avoid separate typed helper functions for legs and instead use a loop over side values [1,-1] directly inline, keeping everything inferred.

input.command: cd ~/tmp-archive/sonnet-100/redPandaSonnet/ && sed -n 1,35p src/builder.ts; grep -n "^  [a-z]*(" src/builder.ts | head -60; sed -n 60,140p src/ik.ts
